candidate.title: Synthetic Pair Finder Fixture
candidate.statement: Find the two different positions in an integer array whose values total the requested target. Return their zero-based indices; either index order is accepted. Each valid input has exactly one unordered answer pair.
constraints: Exactly one valid unordered pair of distinct indices exists.

examples.explanation: The values at positions 0 and 1 total 9.

clarifications.question: May one position be reused?
clarifications.answer: No. Equal values at different positions may be used.

clarifications.question: Can input values repeat?
clarifications.answer: Yes. Distinct positions, not distinct values, are required.

clarifications.question: Can no answer or multiple answers occur?
clarifications.answer: The base contract promises exactly one valid unordered index pair. Changed guarantees belong to variants.

clarifications.question: Does result order matter?
clarifications.answer: Either ordering of the two valid zero-based indices is accepted.

clarifications.question: Is input sorted?
clarifications.answer: No. Preserve original positions if sorting internally.

clarifications.question: Can numbers or target be negative or zero?
May input be modified?
clarifications.answer: No additional immutability requirement is imposed here; original-index semantics must still be preserved.

clarifications.question: Can these sums/complements overflow signed 32-bit integers?
clarifications.answer: No. With values/target within ±1,000,000,000, both sum and complement stay within ±2,000,000,000; this fits signed 32-bit arithmetic.

invariants: Returned indices refer to the original input and must differ.
The base unique-answer guarantee does not authorize no-answer/multiple-answer tests.
Correct unfamiliar approaches are not rejected merely for lacking a reference ID.
Hidden tests, expected hidden outputs and private review notes stay out of conversational context.

approaches.name: Distinct-pair scan
steps: For i in 0..n-1, visit j in i+1..n-1.
preconditions: Base problem constraints and distinct original indices.
approaches.correctness: Every pair of distinct positions appears once, so the promised unique answer is visited.
tradeoffs: Simple baseline; does not meet the subquadratic follow-up.

mistakes.whyIncorrect: The current element can match itself.

hints.text: What work is repeated when you compare every pair?
For a fixed x, what exact partner value would reach target?
How could you remember earlier values together with their positions for quick lookup?
Look for target-x among earlier entries before recording the current value and index. Why does this prevent using the same position twice?

followups.question: How can you improve on comparing every pair?
expectedAnswerPoints: Expected O(n) hashing with O(n) memory, or O(n log n) indexed sorting.
followups.evaluationGuidance: Assess the stated reasoning and assumptions; unfamiliar but valid approaches may be accepted. No unsupported impossibility or speedup claims.
followups.authorshipNote: Adapted and corrected from owner package.

variants.changedContract: Sorted input; define zero- or one-based output before use.
variants.reasoningOnlyReason: Draft follow-up content; full input/output contract, checker and reviewed dedicated test suite are not supplied.

strong: Explains distinct positions, original indexing, duplicates and uniqueness.
incorrect: Returns values or reuses one index.

strong: States a valid invariant and correctness argument.
partial: Knows a pattern but cannot yet justify ordering.
incorrect: Uses unsupported pruning or two pointers on unsorted values.

strong: Accounts for memory, sorting, slicing and expected hash behavior.
partial: Gives the headline bound without assumptions.
incorrect: Treats list insertion as logarithmic or asserts nonexistent overflow.

strong: Adapts to explicitly changed contracts with clear assumptions.
partial: Needs guidance to identify changed guarantees.
incorrect: Applies the base algorithm despite incompatible requirements.

manifest.inputShape: Object containing integer array nums and integer target under base constraints.
manifest.outputShape: Array of exactly two integer zero-based distinct in-range indices; either order.
manifest.comparisonRule: Reject non-integer/bool indices, wrong length, duplicate/out-of-range indices; compare unordered pair to the independently verified expected pair.
